# Third-party scripts, vendored unmodified

## `prepare-iwslt14.sh`

Verbatim copy of fairseq's own IWSLT14 de-en preparation script.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source | https://github.com/pytorch/fairseq/blob/v0.12.2/examples/translation/prepare-iwslt14.sh |
| Retrieved | 2026-08-12 |
| md5 | `c812406528dde9686c97f94768bfcc55` |
| Lines | 115 |
| Modifications | **none** |
| Licence | MIT, as part of fairseq |

Byte-identical to both the `v0.12.2` tag and `main` at the time of retrieval
(checked with `diff`).

**Why vendored rather than downloaded at run time:** pinning it here fixes the
recipe permanently. Fetching from `main` would mean an upstream edit silently
changes our data preprocessing between experiments.

**Why it is not simply used from this repo's own tree:** this Mask-Predict fork
of fairseq 0.7.2 stripped the `examples/` directory, so the script was never
present here. Verified: `git cat-file -e d2cfacc:examples/translation/prepare-iwslt14.sh`
fails.

Run it through `scripts/prepare_iwslt14.sh`, which supplies its dependencies and
then binarises the output. Do not edit this file — the point of it is to be
unmodified.

### What it produces

Verified locally on 2026-08-12, matching the published IWSLT14 de-en figures
exactly:

```
train 160239    valid 7283    test 6750
```

Output is **lowercased** and Moses-tokenised with XML escaping (`'` → `&apos;`),
which is what published IWSLT14 numbers are computed on.
